terms.comment: Traupman’s colloquial “cool!”, Mīrandum est! The gerundive means “to be wondered at, wonderful” (Lewis & Short s.v. mīror); the slang sense is modern.

terms.gloss: grow cool, cool down (of something hot)
evidence: Cato Agr. 105: ubi id vīnum refrīxerit
terms.comment: The intransitive verb: the food cools by itself, where refrīgerō is to cool it. Cato also says frīgēscō: sinitō frīgēscat, let it cool (Agr. 95).

phrases.latin: ubi erit tam crassum quam viscum, sinitō frīgēscat
phrases.english: when it is as thick as birdlime, let it cool
It’s too hot; let it cool down.

phrases.latin: Cum ferbuerit, coctum tollēs ut refrīgēscat.
phrases.english: When it has boiled, take it off the heat to cool.

phrases.latin: Nimis calidum est; sine paulisper refrīgēscat.
phrases.english: It’s too hot; let it cool for a bit.

phrases.latin: Carnem ē furnō exēmimus; sine paulisper quiēscat.
phrases.english: We’ve taken the meat out of the oven; let it rest for a bit.

sources: Lewis & Short: refrigero · Lewis & Short: refrigesco · Lewis & Short: frigesco
